If you're choosing private vs. group swim lessons for a child in Vaughan, I’d generally recommend small-group lessons first unless your child is nervous, significantly behind, or needs very focused instruction.

Private vs. group
	Private	Group / small group
Attention	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 1-on-1	⭐⭐⭐⭐
Skill progression	Usually faster	Steadier
Confidence	Excellent for nervous kids	Good for most kids
Social/fun aspect	Lower	Higher
Cost	Higher	Lower
Learning to swim with others	Less practice	Better
Best for	Fear, catching up, specific skills	Most beginners & developing swimmers
When I'd choose private

Private lessons make sense if your child:

Is afraid of the water or refuses to put their face underwater.
Has tried group lessons and isn't progressing.
Needs to catch up to their peers.
Gets distracted in a group.
Has a specific goal, such as floating independently, breathing, or improving freestyle/backstroke.
You want maximum progress in the shortest amount of pool time.

For example, the YMCA's Vaughan location offers 30-minute private lessons specifically described as personalized, one-on-one instruction.

I'd choose small-group if your child is reasonably comfortable in the water and can follow an instructor.

The big advantage is that kids learn while watching other children, taking turns, and swimming around peers. A 3:1 type of class can be a particularly nice middle ground—much cheaper than private while still giving the instructor plenty of individual attention.

Yes—**hiring a private swim instructor in Pickering can be perfectly safe**, but I’d vet the individual rather than assuming that “swim instructor” automatically means they’re qualified.

 Ontario has specific requirements for aquatic instruction at public pools: instructors should hold a current aquatic-instructor certification and a current lifeguard or assistant-lifeguard certification, or the facility must have a lifeguard supervising the instruction.  Ontario+1

 ### What I would check before hiring

 - **Certifications:** Ask to see their current **Lifesaving Society Swim for Life Instructor** certification and **National Lifeguard** certification (or equivalent).
- **First aid/CPR:** Confirm current **Standard First Aid \+ CPR-C/AED**.
- **Pool location:** A lesson at a properly operated public/club pool is generally preferable to an unfamiliar private residence pool.
- **If it's a child's lesson:** Meet the instructor beforehand, stay nearby during the lesson, and make sure you know exactly who else will be present.
- **Insurance/background screening:** For someone working independently with children, I'd ask whether they carry liability insurance and have a recent vulnerable-sector/background check.
- **Don't pay a large amount upfront** until you've verified the instructor and tried a lesson.
- **Watch the first lesson:** The instructor should have a clear safety plan, stay attentive to the swimmer, and never leave a child unsupervised in or around the water.

 The **City of Pickering itself offers private 1-on-1 lessons** through its Lifesaving Society program, which is a useful benchmark for the qualifications and structure you should expect from a private instructor.  City of Pickering

In Oshawa, the basic difference is **how many swimmers share the instructor’s attention**:

 |  | **Private** | **Semi-private** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Swimmers | 1 swimmer | Usually 2 swimmers |
| Instructor attention | 100% focused on one swimmer | Shared between the two |
| Pace | Completely customized | Somewhat coordinated between swimmers |
| Best for | Beginners, nervous swimmers, specific skill gaps | Siblings/friends with similar abilities |
| Cost | More expensive | Usually cheaper per child |

 For example, **Aqua Elite in Oshawa** offers a 1:1 private option and a 2:1 semi-private option, with individualized skill tracking and feedback.  My Site+1

 ### Which would I choose?

 - **Choose private** if your child is nervous in the water, is significantly behind their peers, needs lots of repetition, or you want the fastest possible improvement.
- **Choose semi-private** if you have **two children around the same swimming level**. They can learn together while still getting considerably more individual attention than in a normal group class.
- If the two swimmers are at **very different levels**, private is generally better because the instructor won't have to split the lesson between competing needs.

 One important distinction: **the City of Oshawa's "Private Swim" program specifically means 1:1 instruction**. Their current program description says participants receive individual attention and can select a preferred day/time.  City of Oshawa+1

Not necessarily. **Private lessons can be safer in some ways, but group lessons can be just as safe when they’re well supervised.** The biggest factors are instructor qualifications, child-to-instructor ratio, pool setup, and supervision—not simply private vs. group.

 - **Private lessons:** One-on-one attention can help an instructor identify weaknesses and intervene quickly. They can also be useful for a child who is anxious or has specific needs.
- **Small-group lessons:** These can provide good instruction while maintaining close supervision, especially with a low student-to-instructor ratio.
- **Large groups:** These generally make it harder for an instructor to monitor every child and may be less appropriate for young or inexperienced swimmers.

 Most importantly, **swim lessons should not be treated as drowning prevention by themselves**. Children still need close, constant supervision around water, even after they learn to swim.

 If you're choosing between a private instructor and a particular group program, I can give you a **safety checklist for evaluating either one**.

If your goal is to **actually become a confident, competent swimmer**, private lessons are usually much better than learning entirely from videos.

 ### Private lessons

 **Best for:** beginners, overcoming fear, fixing technique, learning efficiently.

 - An instructor can spot mistakes you can't see yourself.
- They can teach breathing, body position, floating, kicking, and strokes in the right order.
- You get immediate feedback and corrections.
- They can adapt drills to your specific weaknesses.
- Safety is a major advantage, especially if you're not yet comfortable in deep water.

 **Downside:** more expensive and requires scheduling.

 ### Learning on your own with videos

 **Best for:** someone who already feels comfortable in the water and wants to improve technique.

 - Very cheap or free.
- You can practice whenever you want.
- Plenty of excellent instructional material exists.
- Great for reinforcing things you've learned from an instructor.

 **Downside:** it's easy to practice a mistake repeatedly. Videos also can't tell you _why_ you're struggling with your breathing, body position, or stroke.

 ### My recommendation

 If you're a **complete beginner**, I'd do **3–6 private lessons**, then practice on your own between/after lessons using videos.

 That gives you the best of both worlds: an instructor establishes the fundamentals and corrects your technique, while independent practice builds endurance and confidence.

For a **private swim lesson at your house**, I’d have these ready:

 - 🩱 **Swimsuit** and towel for the swimmer
- 🥽 **Goggles** if they use them
- 🧴 **Sunscreen** for outdoor pools
- 💧 **Water bottle** and a small snack for afterward
- 🩴 **Flip-flops or pool shoes**
- 🏊 **Pool access** — make sure the gate is unlocked and the instructor can easily get to the pool
- 🌡️ **Comfortable pool temperature** — especially important for young children
- 🧹 **Clear pool deck** — remove toys, furniture, hoses, and anything someone could trip over
- 🚿 **Bathroom/changing area** available
- 🩹 **Basic first-aid supplies** nearby
- 📋 **Any relevant information for the instructor**, such as swimming experience, comfort level, goals, or anything they're nervous about

 ### If it’s a child’s first lesson

 It can help to tell them beforehand that the instructor will be there to **teach and practice**, not to test them. Avoid pressuring them to get in or perform a particular skill.

 Also, if the instructor is coming to your home, **confirm the lesson time, duration, payment, cancellation policy, and what equipment they provide** beforehand.
